text: A sentence devoid of expectancy and other [essential qualities] is not a valid means of knowledge. For example, "cow, horse, man, elephant" is not a valid means of knowledge due to the absence of expectancy. "Sprinkle with fire" is not a valid means of knowledge due to the absence of compatibility. Words such as "bring the cow," spoken after a long interval, are not a valid means of knowledge due to the absence of proximity.
